src/application/assign-task-use-case.ts: `typeof dto.assigneeId !== "string"` only checks the DTO's shape. It is not a domain rule.
src/application/assign-task-use-case.ts: `task.assignTo(dto.assigneeId)` hands the assignment rule to the domain entity.
src/application/assign-task-use-case.ts: `await this.tasks.save(task)` saves through the repository interface, not through concrete persistence code.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: AssignTaskUseCase does the job an application-layer use case is supposed to do. It loads the task through the TaskRepository port, checks the assignee exists through the UserRepository port, hands the state change to the domain method task.assignTo, and saves the result. The typeof check on dto.assigneeId only checks the shape of the incoming DTO. The two existence checks are lookups across aggregates, which is normal coordination for a use case. Neither is a business invariant that has leaked out of the domain. The file contains no persistence code, transport or HTTP handling, or framework code, and it doesn't decide how a task gets assigned. That rule stays in Task.assignTo. No ADR text was provided to compare against.
